Share the same page flag bit for PG_readahead and PG_reclaim.
One is used only on file reads, another is only for emergency writes.  One
is used mostly for fresh/young pages, another is for old pages.
a) clear PG_reclaim => implicit clear of PG_readahead

column2: it will delay an asynchronous readahead into a synchronous one

column3: the pages will be reclaimed soon, it's readahead thrashing!
in this case, synchronous readahead makes more sense.

column1: b) clear PG_readahead => implicit clear of PG_reclaim

column2: one(and only one) page will not be reclaimed in time
it can be avoided by checking PageWriteback(page) in readahead first

column1: c) set PG_reclaim => implicit set of PG_readahead

column2: will confuse readahead and make it restart the size rampup process
it's a trivial problem, and can mostly be avoided by checking

column1: d) set PG_readahead => implicit set of PG_reclaim

column2: PG_readahead will never be set on already cached pages.
